courses.title: HVAC System Essentials
moduleTitles: Introducing Air Conditioning High Side Components

questions.prompt: What does vehicle air conditioning mainly do to cabin air?
questions.explanation: A/C transfers heat out of the cabin; evaporator cooling also condenses moisture from the air.

options.label: A
options.body: Heats the air and raises its humidity

options.label: B
options.body: Moves heat from inside the cabin to outside the vehicle, cooling and dehumidifying the air

options.label: C
options.body: Creates cold air inside the compressor

options.label: D
options.body: Removes all oxygen from the cabin

questions.prompt: In the refrigeration cycle, refrigerant absorbs heat in the cabin and releases heat outside when it:
questions.explanation: Low-pressure evaporation absorbs heat; compression and high-pressure condensation reject it outside.

options.label: A
options.body: Stays as a liquid at constant pressure throughout

options.label: B
options.body: Evaporates at low pressure in the evaporator, then is compressed and condenses at high pressure in the condenser

options.label: C
options.body: Freezes in the condenser

options.label: D
options.body: Burns in the compressor

questions.prompt: Why is the change of state of the refrigerant so important to A/C operation?
questions.explanation: Latent heat in boiling/condensing moves far more heat than temperature change alone.

options.label: A
options.body: It changes the colour of the refrigerant

options.label: B
options.body: A liquid boiling to vapour absorbs a large amount of heat, and vapour condensing back to liquid releases that heat

options.label: C
options.body: It makes the refrigerant heavier

options.label: D
options.body: It stops the compressor from turning

questions.prompt: The high side of the system runs from:
questions.moduleTitle: Introducing Air Conditioning High Side Components
questions.explanation: The high side is the high-pressure, hot section: compressor outlet to metering device inlet.

options.label: A
options.body: The evaporator outlet back to the expansion device

options.label: B
options.body: The compressor discharge, through the condenser, to the inlet of the expansion device / orifice

options.label: C
options.body: The cabin filter to the blower motor

options.label: D
options.body: The radiator to the heater core

questions.prompt: What is the job of the condenser?
questions.moduleTitle: Introducing Air Conditioning High Side Components
questions.explanation: The condenser cools the discharge vapour so it condenses, giving up its heat to outside air.

options.label: A
options.body: To absorb heat from cabin air

options.label: B
options.body: To reject heat to outside air, changing hot high-pressure vapour into high-pressure liquid

options.label: C
options.body: To expand the refrigerant and drop its pressure

options.label: D
options.body: To store liquid refrigerant for the low side only

questions.prompt: A blocked condenser airflow (debris, failed fan) will most directly cause:
questions.moduleTitle: Introducing Air Conditioning High Side Components
questions.explanation: If the condenser cannot reject heat, pressure and temperature climb and cooling suffers.

options.label: A
options.body: Low-side pressure to fall to zero at all times

options.label: B
options.body: High-side pressure and temperature to rise, with poor cooling

options.label: C
options.body: The evaporator to flood with liquid

options.label: D
options.body: The compressor clutch air gap to increase

questions.prompt: What happens inside the evaporator?
questions.explanation: The evaporator is where cold low-pressure refrigerant evaporates and cools cabin air.

options.label: A
options.body: High-pressure liquid is stored

options.label: B
options.body: Low-pressure liquid refrigerant boils and absorbs heat from air passing over the fins

options.label: C
options.body: Refrigerant is compressed

options.label: D
options.body: Refrigerant gives up heat to outside air

questions.prompt: Just before the evaporator, the expansion device (TXV or fixed orifice) causes:
questions.explanation: Metering the liquid creates the pressure drop that makes the evaporator cold.

options.label: A
options.body: A rise in pressure and temperature

options.label: B
options.body: A sharp drop in pressure, so the refrigerant entering the evaporator is cold and low-pressure

options.label: C
options.body: The refrigerant to become a superheated vapour

options.label: D
options.body: The compressor to stop

questions.prompt: Before opening any A/C system, refrigerant must be:
questions.explanation: Refrigerant is recovered, never vented; recharge is by the specified weight after evacuation.

options.label: A
options.body: Vented to the atmosphere

options.label: B
options.body: Recovered into approved equipment, then the system can be opened, repaired, evacuated, and recharged by weight

options.label: C
options.body: Diluted with water

options.label: D
options.body: Mixed with engine oil and drained

questions.prompt: Why is a deep vacuum (evacuation) held on an opened system before recharging?
questions.explanation: Evacuation removes non-condensables and moisture that harm performance and components.

options.label: A
options.body: To inflate the hoses

options.label: B
options.body: To remove air and boil off moisture, which would otherwise form acids, cause icing, and reduce cooling

options.label: C
options.body: To add oil to the compressor

options.label: D
options.body: To test the cabin filter

questions.prompt: Which set is correctly all HVAC sensor inputs?
questions.explanation: Sensors report temperatures, sun load, and pressure to the HVAC module; motors and clutches are outputs.

options.label: A
options.body: Blower motor, blend door actuator, compressor clutch

options.label: B
options.body: In-car temperature, ambient temperature, evaporator temperature, sun load, and refrigerant pressure sensors

options.label: C
options.body: Radiator fan, heater valve, recirculation flap motor

options.label: D
options.body: Windshield washer level and fuel level

questions.prompt: The evaporator temperature sensor is used mainly to:
questions.explanation: If the evaporator gets too cold, frost blocks airflow; its sensor lets the module prevent freeze-up.

options.label: A
options.body: Measure engine coolant temperature

options.label: B
options.body: Prevent evaporator icing by cycling or controlling the compressor before the evaporator freezes

options.label: C
options.body: Lock the doors automatically

options.label: D
options.body: Measure road speed

questions.prompt: A faulty refrigerant pressure sensor signal can cause the HVAC module to:
questions.explanation: Out-of-range pressure readings lead the module to disable the compressor for protection.

options.label: A
options.body: Increase tire pressure

options.label: B
options.body: Inhibit compressor engagement if pressure reads too high or too low, to protect the system

options.label: C
options.body: Turn off the headlights only

options.label: D
options.body: Open the thermostat

questions.prompt: In automatic climate control, the HVAC control module decides blower speed, air distribution, and temperature by:
questions.explanation: Automatic control compares target vs. measured conditions and adjusts outputs continuously.

options.label: A
options.body: Guessing randomly each time the engine starts

options.label: B
options.body: Combining the set temperature with sensor inputs and then driving the outputs to reach and hold that temperature

options.label: C
options.body: Following only the position of the blower switch

options.label: D
options.body: Turning every output fully on at all times

questions.prompt: Selecting recirculation instead of fresh air helps most when:
questions.explanation: Recirculating already-cooled cabin air speeds pull-down; fresh air is better for demisting.

options.label: A
options.body: Maximum cooling is needed on a very hot day or outside air is smoky/dirty, because cabin air is reused

options.label: B
options.body: The windshield needs demisting in wet weather

options.label: C
options.body: The engine is cold and needs warming

options.label: D
options.body: The vehicle is being pressure washed

questions.prompt: A blend (temperature) door that does not respond to a temperature change request is a fault in which part of the control loop?
questions.explanation: The module may command correctly, but a failed actuator/circuit/door prevents the output moving.

options.label: A
options.body: Only the refrigerant charge

options.label: B
options.body: The link between the control decision and the output - the blend door actuator, its circuit, or the door itself

options.label: C
options.body: The condenser fan only

options.label: D
options.body: The sun load sensor lens colour

questions.prompt: Which of these is an HVAC output controlled by the module?
questions.explanation: Blower, doors, and compressor control are driven outputs; sensors are inputs.

options.label: A
options.body: Ambient temperature sensor

options.label: B
options.body: Blower motor speed, mode/blend door actuators, and compressor clutch or variable compressor control

options.label: C
options.body: Refrigerant pressure sensor

options.label: D
options.body: Sun load sensor

questions.prompt: On a variable-displacement compressor with no clutch, cooling output is varied by:
questions.explanation: Clutchless compressors vary stroke/displacement electrically instead of cycling a clutch.

options.label: A
options.body: Removing the drive belt

options.label: B
options.body: A control valve/solenoid that changes compressor displacement in response to module command

options.label: C
options.body: The cabin filter

options.label: D
options.body: Changing tire size

questions.prompt: R1234YF was introduced mainly as a replacement for R134a because it has:
questions.explanation: R1234yf has very low GWP compared with R134a and similar operating characteristics.

options.label: A
options.body: Much higher global warming potential

options.label: B
options.body: A much lower global warming potential, while working at similar pressures

options.label: C
options.body: No need for any oil

options.label: D
options.body: A completely different refrigeration cycle with no condenser

questions.prompt: Which servicing point about R1234YF is correct?
questions.explanation: R1234yf is A2L mildly flammable, has distinct fittings, and requires dedicated equipment and procedures.

options.label: A
options.body: It can be freely mixed with R134a in any system

options.label: B
options.body: It is mildly flammable (A2L), uses its own service fittings and dedicated recovery/recharge equipment, and must not be mixed with R134a

options.label: C
options.body: It needs no leak testing

options.label: D
options.body: Any R134a machine can be used with no changes

questions.prompt: A correct performance check starts by:
questions.explanation: Comparable results need the manufacturer's test conditions and stabilised readings.

options.label: A
options.body: Immediately adding refrigerant

options.label: B
options.body: Setting the controls as specified (usually max/cold A/C, recirculation, set blower and engine RPM), noting ambient temperature and humidity, and letting pressures and vent temperature stabilise

options.label: C
options.body: Removing the condenser fan

options.label: D
options.body: Driving at motorway speed with the windows open

questions.prompt: Centre vent temperature is measured best with:
questions.explanation: A probe in the vent airstream, judged against the ambient-based spec, is the reliable check.

options.label: A
options.body: An infrared gun pointed at the dashboard plastic

options.label: B
options.body: A probe thermometer inserted in the centre vent, compared with the specified value for the ambient temperature

options.label: C
options.body: A finger held in front of the vent

options.label: D
options.body: The engine coolant gauge

questions.prompt: Vent temperature is warmer than specified but both gauge pressures are near normal. A good next check is:
questions.explanation: Near-normal pressures point away from the refrigeration loop toward air-side and door faults.

options.label: A
options.body: Condemn the compressor at once

options.label: B
options.body: Check for a blend door not reaching full cold, heater valve/heater bleed-through, or a restricted cabin filter/airflow fault

options.label: C
options.body: Add double the specified charge

options.label: D
options.body: Replace the condenser without testing

questions.prompt: Why must ambient temperature and humidity be recorded during a performance check?
questions.explanation: A vent temp that is normal at 35C ambient would be poor at 20C; conditions set the expectation.

options.label: A
options.body: They change the colour of the gauges

options.label: B
options.body: Expected vent temperature and pressures rise with ambient heat and humidity, so a reading can only be judged against its conditions

options.label: C
options.body: They determine the engine oil grade

options.label: D
options.body: They have no effect on A/C performance

questions.prompt: During the check, the condenser fan does not run with A/C on. The likely effect on the readings is:
questions.explanation: Without condenser airflow at idle, heat rejection falls, head pressure rises, and cooling drops.

options.label: A
options.body: Lower high-side pressure and colder vent air

options.label: B
options.body: Higher high-side pressure and warmer vent air, especially at idle

options.label: C
options.body: No change at any speed

options.label: D
options.body: Low-side pressure only, with no other change

questions.prompt: A system passes the vent-temperature check at fast idle but is poor in slow traffic. This pattern most suggests:
questions.explanation: Speed-dependent cooling points to airflow over the condenser, which road speed provides but traffic does not.

options.label: A
options.body: A fault that appears only under load - check condenser airflow/fan operation and air in the system

options.label: B
options.body: The system is fully normal and needs no checks

options.label: C
options.body: The cabin filter is new

options.label: D
options.body: The refrigerant is overcharged with oil only

questions.prompt: Touch/temperature checks along the lines during a performance test can help locate:
questions.explanation: An unexpected cold spot or frost marks a restriction creating a pressure drop.

options.label: A
options.body: A radio fault

options.label: B
options.body: A restriction - a sharp temperature drop or frosting at one point where there should not be one

options.label: C
options.body: Low tire pressure

options.label: D
options.body: A worn wheel bearing

questions.prompt: After a repair, the correct way to confirm the fix is to:
questions.explanation: Repeating the standardised check proves the repair restored specified performance.

options.label: A
options.body: Ask the customer to test it over the next month

options.label: B
options.body: Repeat the full performance check under the same conditions and confirm vent temperature and pressures are now within specification

options.label: C
options.body: Only check that the clutch engages

options.label: D
options.body: Clear the fault codes and release the vehicle

questions.prompt: Superheat/subcooling or line temperatures well outside the expected range during a check most likely indicate:
questions.explanation: Abnormal superheat/subcooling points to charge or loop faults that gauges and temps together help isolate.

options.label: A
options.body: A fault with charge level or a component/restriction in the refrigeration loop - investigate before re-gassing by guesswork

options.label: B
options.body: That the thermometer battery is flat in all cases

options.label: C
options.body: A fault in the audio system

options.label: D
options.body: That performance checking is not needed

questions.prompt: A very cold suction line with frost back to the compressor during the check can indicate:
questions.explanation: Frost to the compressor risks liquid slugging; metering device and charge must be checked.

options.label: A
options.body: Normal operation on every system

options.label: B
options.body: Overfeeding / expansion device stuck open or incorrect charge, risking liquid returning to the compressor

options.label: C
options.body: A blocked condenser

options.label: D
options.body: A flat battery

questions.prompt: With the system running, BOTH low-side and high-side pressures are lower than normal and cooling is poor. The most likely cause is:
questions.explanation: Low charge starves both sides; find and repair the leak, then recharge by weight.

options.label: A
options.body: Overcharge

options.label: B
options.body: Undercharge (low refrigerant, often from a leak)

options.label: C
options.body: A blocked condenser

options.label: D
options.body: Air in the system

questions.prompt: Both pressures are HIGHER than normal with poor cooling on a hot day. Which cause fits best?
questions.explanation: Excess charge, non-condensables, or poor heat rejection all drive both pressures up.

options.label: A
options.body: Undercharge

options.label: B
options.body: Overcharge, air in the system, or poor condenser airflow/cooling

options.label: C
options.body: A completely empty system

options.label: D
options.body: A failed evaporator blower only

questions.prompt: Low-side pressure is very low (near vacuum) while high-side is low/normal and the evaporator outlet is cold at one spot. This points to:
questions.explanation: Starved evaporator flow pulls suction down; a restriction or icing metering device is likely.

options.label: A
options.body: A restriction in the low side / metering device or a moisture-iced expansion device

options.label: B
options.body: An overcharge

options.label: C
options.body: A slipping clutch only

options.label: D
options.body: A faulty sun load sensor

questions.prompt: High-side pressure is very high but low-side is near normal, with the liquid line hot. A likely cause is:
questions.explanation: A high-side blockage backs pressure up ahead of it while the low side can still look near normal.

options.label: A
options.body: A restriction on the high side, such as a blocked condenser or kinked liquid line

options.label: B
options.body: A system with no compressor drive

options.label: C
options.body: A blown cabin fuse

options.label: D
options.body: A worn blower resistor

questions.prompt: Static (engine off, system equalised) pressure is far below the value expected for the ambient temperature. That tells you:
questions.explanation: Equalised static pressure vs. ambient reveals a low/empty system before the engine is started.

options.label: A
options.body: The compressor is faulty

options.label: B
options.body: There is little or no refrigerant charge - leak-test before any running tests

options.label: C
options.body: The TXV is stuck open

options.label: D
options.body: The clutch gap is too wide

questions.prompt: The compressor clutch will not engage. Before condemning the clutch coil, first confirm:
questions.explanation: Many no-engage faults are missing command, feed, or ground - not a failed coil.

options.label: A
options.body: The tire pressures

options.label: B
options.body: That the module is commanding engagement and that power and ground actually reach the clutch connector

options.label: C
options.body: The radio volume

options.label: D
options.body: The cabin filter condition

questions.prompt: Power and ground are present at the clutch, but it still does not pull in. Measuring the coil shows an open circuit. The diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Feed and ground proven good plus an open coil confirms the coil itself has failed.

options.label: A
options.body: A faulty condenser fan

options.label: B
options.body: A failed (open) clutch coil - replace the coil/clutch assembly as specified

options.label: C
options.body: Low refrigerant charge

options.label: D
options.body: A blocked receiver drier

questions.prompt: The clutch engages but slips, squeals, and gets hot, with a burnt face. A common mechanical cause to check is:
questions.explanation: Wide gap, worn faces, and high compressor torque all make the clutch slip and overheat.

options.label: A
options.body: Excessive clutch air gap, a worn/contaminated clutch face, or a partially seizing compressor raising the load

options.label: B
options.body: Too much refrigerant oil in the cabin

options.label: C
options.body: A new drive belt

options.label: D
options.body: High blower speed

questions.prompt: What does the clutch air gap measurement check?
questions.explanation: Air gap must be in specification for reliable engagement without dragging.

options.label: A
options.body: The distance between the condenser and radiator

options.label: B
options.body: The gap between the clutch plate and pulley - too wide weakens magnetic pull-in, too narrow can cause drag when disengaged

options.label: C
options.body: The gap in the spark plugs

options.label: D
options.body: The evaporator fin spacing

questions.prompt: The clutch cycles on and off very rapidly (short-cycling). Which checks belong in the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Short-cycling is usually commanded in response to pressure or evaporator temperature signals, or low charge.

options.label: A
options.body: Only the clutch relay paint colour

options.label: B
options.body: Refrigerant charge / pressure readings and the evaporator temperature and pressure switch/sensor signals that command cycling

options.label: C
options.body: Wiper blade size

options.label: D
options.body: Wheel alignment

questions.prompt: An air conditioning thermistor (thermal mistore) is:
questions.explanation: Thermistors convert temperature into a resistance/voltage signal the module can read.

options.label: A
options.body: A fixed resistor that never changes value

options.label: B
options.body: A temperature-sensitive resistor whose resistance changes in a known way with temperature, used to sense evaporator or cabin air temperature

options.label: C
options.body: A type of compressor clutch

options.label: D
options.body: A pressure switch with two fixed contacts

questions.prompt: Most automotive temperature thermistors are NTC type. NTC means that as temperature rises:
questions.explanation: Negative Temperature Coefficient: hotter = lower resistance, which the module reads as a rising signal voltage in a typical pull-up circuit.

options.label: A
options.body: Resistance rises sharply

options.label: B
options.body: Resistance falls

options.label: C
options.body: Resistance stays exactly the same

options.label: D
options.body: The sensor produces its own voltage like a battery

questions.prompt: An evaporator thermistor reads open circuit. The HVAC module will most likely interpret this as:
questions.explanation: An open sensor drives the signal to one extreme; live data vs. actual temperature exposes the fault.

options.label: A
options.body: An extremely cold or extremely warm evaporator (depending on circuit design) and may inhibit or mis- control the compressor - compare scan temperature with actual measured temperature

options.label: B
options.body: A correct reading needing no action

options.label: C
options.body: Low refrigerant pressure

options.label: D
options.body: A condenser fan fault

questions.prompt: To test a thermistor properly, you should:
questions.explanation: Resistance-at-temperature against the spec chart, plus a smooth change, proves or condemns the sensor.

options.label: A
options.body: Only check that its connector is plugged in

options.label: B
options.body: Measure its resistance at a known temperature (or compare scan-tool temperature with a thermometer at the sensor) and check it changes smoothly as temperature changes

options.label: C
options.body: Apply battery voltage directly across it

options.label: D
options.body: Short it to ground and watch for sparks

questions.prompt: A 'sun load sensor voltage low' fault means the module sees the signal:
questions.explanation: Voltage low codes set when the signal sits below the plausible window, typically a short to ground or sensor failure.

options.label: A
options.body: Above its 5V reference at all times

options.label: B
options.body: Below the expected minimum - near 0V - suggesting a short to ground in the signal wire, a failed sensor pulling the signal down, or a lost reference/ground fault, depending on circuit design

options.label: C
options.body: Exactly at the correct value for bright sun

options.label: D
options.body: Only when the headlights are on

questions.prompt: The sun load sensor's normal job is to:
questions.explanation: Sun load lets auto climate compensate for solar heating before cabin temperature drifts.

options.label: A
options.body: Measure refrigerant pressure

options.label: B
options.body: Measure sunlight intensity on the cabin so automatic climate control can add cooling for the side/load the sun is heating

options.label: C
options.body: Measure vehicle speed

options.label: D
options.body: Sense rain on the windshield

questions.prompt: With the sensor unplugged, the signal wire measures a good reference voltage and ground is good, but plugged in the signal collapses to near 0V. This points to:
questions.explanation: Feed and ground proven good unplugged, signal pulled down when connected, implicates the sensor.

options.label: A
options.body: A faulty sensor itself shorting the signal internally

options.label: B
options.body: An open signal wire

options.label: C
options.body: A faulty blower motor

options.label: D
options.body: Low refrigerant charge

questions.prompt: A 'sun load sensor voltage high' fault means the module sees the signal:
questions.explanation: Voltage high codes set when the signal is pulled up toward reference by an open/short-to-voltage fault.

options.label: A
options.body: Stuck at the value for total darkness and correct

options.label: B
options.body: At or near the reference voltage / above the expected maximum - suggesting an open signal or ground circuit, an unplugged sensor, or a short to voltage

options.label: C
options.body: Below 0.2V at all times

options.label: D
options.body: Only on cloudy days

questions.prompt: A sun load sensor is unplugged during other work and the A/C is then tested. The most likely result is:
questions.explanation: An open connector is a classic voltage-high cause; restore the connection and retest the live signal in light and shade.

options.label: A
options.body: No fault of any kind

options.label: B
options.body: A voltage high fault may set, and automatic climate loses sun compensation until the sensor is reconnected and the code cleared/retested

options.label: C
options.body: The compressor will seize

options.label: D
options.body: The evaporator will freeze solid immediately

questions.prompt: To distinguish a wiring fault from a sensor fault on a voltage-high code, the best test is:
questions.explanation: Prove the three wires first; a good sensor signal must vary between covered (dark) and bright light.

options.label: A
options.body: Replace the HVAC module first

options.label: B
options.body: Check the signal, reference, and ground at the sensor connector, then test/replace the sensor only if wiring values are correct, and confirm the live signal changes when the sensor is covered and uncovered

options.label: C
options.body: Add refrigerant

options.label: D
options.body: Replace the compressor clutch
